description: A vibrato: a delay line whose length is swept by an internal oscillator, with the dry signal mixable back in to flange

params.text: Sets the rate of the sweep, from 1Hz to 20Hz
Sets the depth of the sweep, from 1ms to 20ms of delay
Mixes the dry signal back in on top of the delayed one, from none to all of it, which turns the vibrato into a flanger
Scales what the depth CV jack adds, 5V covering the whole depth range at its maximum
Scales what the rate CV jack adds, 5V covering the whole rate range at its maximum
Scales what the dry-mix CV jack adds, 5V covering the whole mix range at its maximum

inputs.text: Adds to the depth, scaled by its attenuator, with the total clamped between 1ms and 20ms
Adds to the rate, scaled by its attenuator, with the total clamped between 1Hz and 20Hz
Adds to the dry mix, scaled by its attenuator, with the total clamped between none and all

outputs.text: The delayed signal, with the dry signal added according to the FLANGE controls

notes: there is no feedback path, so the flanging is the shallow kind that comes from one delayed copy meeting the original.
the depth is smoothed with a 5Hz filter before it is used, so a sudden jump in the WIDTH controls glides rather than clicks.
each of the three large knobs draws a gold arc from its own position round to where its CV input and attenuator have moved it, and the arc turns orange when the CV pushes past the knob's limit.
